meta.title: Inflation Just Dropped Hard. Here's the Part Nobody's Talking About.
meta.hook: Inflation just fell off a cliff.
meta.description: US inflation fell from 4.2% to 3.5% in June 2026 — the biggest one-month cooldown in years. Gas crashed 9.7%. But the number that actually matters is core inflation, and it came in flat for the first time outside a recession since 2017. Here's what happened, why it matters, and the date to watch next.

scenes.narration: Inflation just fell off a cliff. And it wasn't the Fed that did it.

visual.query: red inflation line chart plunging sharply downward on a trading terminal
visual.visual_intent: A large financial terminal screen showing a red CPI line chart plunging steeply downward, dark trading floor bokeh behind it, cinematic photoreal Bloomberg documentary look, cold blue and red light
broll_keywords: stock market chart falling red screen
visual.decision_reason: exact recreation: the CPI plunge itself, hook beat, no fade-in

scenes.narration: In June, US inflation dropped from four point two percent to three point five. That's the biggest one-month cooldown since twenty twenty.

visual.query: Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI report headline 3.5 percent
visual.visual_intent: A clean government statistics release on screen with the figure 3.5% prominent, US Bureau of Labor Statistics styling, shallow depth of field, photoreal documentary
visual.decision_reason: exact figure from the June 2026 BLS CPI release

scenes.narration: The reason? Gas. Gasoline prices crashed almost ten percent in a single month. Energy overall fell nearly six.

visual.query: gas station price sign numbers falling american
visual.visual_intent: An American gas station price board with prices visibly low, cars fueling, late afternoon light, real documentary footage
visual.decision_reason: everyday-realism beat: real footage, not AI

scenes.narration: But here's the part almost nobody's talking about. Core inflation — everything except food and gas — came in completely flat. The lowest reading outside a recession since twenty seventeen.

visual.query: flat horizontal line on an economic chart, core inflation unchanged
visual.visual_intent: A stark economic chart where a volatile line suddenly flattens into a perfectly horizontal segment, minimal dark background, glowing white line, cinematic data documentary
visual.decision_reason: the curiosity payoff — the real story beneath the headline number

scenes.narration: Even rent barely moved. Up one tenth of one percent — the smallest jump since twenty twenty-one.

visual.query: american apartment buildings for rent sign residential street
visual.visual_intent: A row of American apartment buildings with a visible 'For Rent' sign, warm evening light, real documentary footage

scenes.narration: So is inflation beaten? Not yet. The Fed is split — some officials still want to hike. The next report lands August twelfth. Follow K70 Network Solution so you see it first.

visual.decision_reason: authority close + forward hook to the Aug 12 print
